dimension_justifications.soundness: Within its tightly defined Qwen3.5/vLLM/Transformers configuration, the paper gives unusually explicit ownership predicates, factorial controls, phase records, selected independent operator checks, and live fault injections (Sections 3-5; Tables 6, 9, 11, and 16). However, the evidence remains conditional on trusted capture, lacks terminal executed-source closure, identifies no compiled Triton binary/autotuning choice, and validates only selected captured-input boundaries rather than end-to-end behavior (pp. 5-7, 10-11, 17, and 21). These limitations are candidly stated but materially constrain the general soundness of the proposed audit as a broadly effective method.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper is lucid, technically careful, and commendably precise about what each table does and does not establish. Figures 1-3 and Tables 7-9 make the contract and evidence boundary inspectable. Nonetheless, the main text runs through page 11 before references start on page 12, exceeding the rubric's nine-page initial-submission main-text limit. Repeated caveats and multiple contextual cohorts also make the core contribution harder to isolate.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The integration of heterogeneous-state ownership witnesses, lifecycle records, digest-based semantic relations, and fault-gated replay is potentially useful. But the paper explicitly acknowledges that the constituent mechanisms are established and offers one frozen reference implementation rather than evidence that ForkAudit improves over existing systems tests, finds previously unknown defects, transfers to another hybrid stack, or provides a reusable broadly validated methodology (pp. 2-3 and Appendix G). Thus its novelty and field-level significance remain uncertain.

paper_summary: ForkAudit is an executable audit contract for branching hybrid LLM requests with token-indexed attention KV state and mutable Gated DeltaNet state. It evaluates four KV/GDN ownership setups across eight PG-19 books and fan-outs of 1, 8, and 32 in one Qwen3.5-35B-A3B stack, checks recorded storage ownership and semantic digest equivalence, tests selected attention and recurrent transitions with independent FP32 calculations, injects nine targeted faults, and separately reports bounded memory and deployment-context measurements.
strongest_verified_contribution: For the specified sequential Qwen3.5/vLLM/Transformers setup, the strongest verified result is a clearly scoped ownership-lifecycle case study: all four registered setup policies match on recorded tokens, CPU-FP32 logit digests, logical KV, and final GDN state across 96 configurations, while phase witnesses report post-transition request/base and request/peer disjointness (Section 5.4; Figure 3; Table 9).
strengths: The paper distinguishes immutable prefix state, private append state, and recurrent-state rebinding rather than treating cache sharing as a single undifferentiated mechanism (Sections 3-4).
The experimental claims are unusually well bounded: Tables 8 and 9 explicitly map cohorts and evidence types to permitted inferences.

The selected dense-FP32 attention oracle and candidate-import-free NumPy GDN recurrence are meaningful checks beyond cross-arm self-consistency, with numerical thresholds and results reported in Sections 5.5-5.6 and Table 16.
Memory accounting is disciplined: allocated-page and allocator measurements are separated from unmeasured NVML/process/service capacity (Section 4.4; Table 6; Appendix E).
The paper avoids overstating its contextual deployment results and explicitly separates them from the primary ownership factorial (Tables 3-5).
questions: Can the authors demonstrate ForkAudit on at least one additional hybrid model/runtime, including an optimized recurrent implementation and a genuinely concurrent or batched execution schedule?
Can the authors evaluate the audit against held-out mutations or naturally occurring regressions, and compare its detection value with a conventional ownership/unit/integration-test suite?

Can the final artifact provide a reproducible executed-source closure and a binding to the compiled attention binary/autotuning configuration, rather than only Python-callable provenance and captured receipts?
Why should the Table 4 Q16 CoMem row remain a headline contextual comparison after the paper reports a same-dtype fork-alias risk for that path?

issues.location: PDF pp. 1-11 main text; references begin on p. 12
issues.observed_evidence: The paper's Introduction begins on PDF p. 1 and its Conclusion ends on PDF p. 11; the References heading begins on p. 12. The supplied rubric requires initial-submission main text of at most nine pages, excluding references and appendices.
issues.why_it_matters: This is an explicit ICLR-format compliance failure and also allows substantial contextual and methodological material that should be compressed or moved to the appendix.
issues.required_fix: Reduce the main text to at most nine pages under the official template, moving nonessential contextual deployment discussion, repeated caveats, and extended protocol detail to the appendix without changing substantive claims.
issues.verification_test: Compile the anonymized final PDF with the official template and verify that all non-reference, non-appendix material occupies no more than nine numbered pages.
issues.evidence_needed: A page-limited final PDF and a clear main-text/appendix boundary.

issues.observed_evidence: The positive ownership evidence uses one Qwen3.5 configuration, one 16-bit KV geometry, one partial-tail length, one sequential round-major CUDA-stream schedule, and selected attention rows/four GDN layers. The nine mutations were selected to target predeclared gates; the paper states that they are positive controls and not completeness evidence (pp. 6-7, 9-11, and 21).
issues.why_it_matters: The central contribution is an audit methodology, but the current study chiefly shows that one bespoke harness can certify its own selected predicates on one implementation. It does not establish transfer, incremental utility over conventional testing, or detection effectiveness against unanticipated faults.
issues.required_fix: Add preregistered transfer experiments on another hybrid stack or model, including concurrent/batched behavior, and a held-out fault or real-regression evaluation compared with ordinary tests. State detection denominators and failure modes explicitly.
issues.verification_test: Independently replay both stacks; require the same contract checks to pass on clean cases, require held-out faults to be detected at their specified predicates, and report comparative detection outcomes against the baseline tests.
issues.evidence_needed: A second-stack artifact, a held-out fault/regression set, and a baseline-testing comparison with complete outcomes.

issues.observed_evidence: The paper reports that post-ledger pycache files broke terminal code-tree closure, that the derivative binds raw bytes and replay rather than a closed original-run identifier, and that dispatch provenance does not fingerprint the compiled Triton binary or autotuning choice (p. 11; Table 9 on p. 17; Appendix I). Most tensor evidence is represented by digests rather than full archived arrays.
issues.why_it_matters: These are direct limitations on an 'executable ownership audit': receipts can support conditional replay but cannot establish that the captured run used the claimed complete source and low-level execution path. This limits independent auditing of the central systems claim.
issues.required_fix: Release or describe a signed, closed executed-source/container manifest; bind compiled-kernel and configuration identities where feasible; preserve enough numerical sidecars for independent recomputation of a representative end-to-end path.
issues.verification_test: Build and run from the released closure in a clean environment; reject altered source, kernel/configuration bindings, and sidecar substitutions before replay; reproduce the registered aggregate.
issues.evidence_needed: A closed executable provenance package and clean-room replay log.

issues.observed_evidence: Table 4 presents a Q16 CoMem row alongside the main comparison, while the text and caption state that a later audit found a same-dtype fork-alias risk and retain it only as single-build/single-query context.
issues.why_it_matters: The caveat is transparent but easy to miss in a performance-style table, potentially encouraging comparison of a known-risk path with the other methods.
issues.required_fix: Visually separate, gray out, or move the Q16 row to a caveated appendix table; foreground the unaffected Q8/Q4 results in the main table.
issues.verification_test: A reader should be able to identify the non-production-risk rows from the table itself without relying on surrounding prose.

ethics_concerns: No direct human-subject, privacy, or safety experiment is apparent. The stated PG-19 training-split usage and broader deployment-scale concern are appropriately acknowledged in the ethics statement (PDF p. 14).
llm_usage_disclosure: This internal review was generated with LLM assistance from the supplied PDF and review rubric only; no external sources, repository files, prior reviews, or author information were consulted.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A compliant nine-page main paper with the core contract and evidence boundary retained.
Independent transfer to another hybrid model/runtime and concurrent or batched serving schedule.
A preregistered held-out fault or naturally occurring regression study showing incremental detection value relative to conventional tests.
A closed, clean-room reproducible execution package that binds the executed source and low-level kernel/configuration provenance.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Failure to reproduce the reported ownership predicates or semantic-digest equivalence from the disclosed receipts.
Evidence that live faults do not consistently trigger their intended predicates under independently rebuilt clean controls.
Evidence that the Q16 alias issue affects the reported Q8/Q4 or primary ownership-factorial results.
Inability to make the submission compliant with the nine-page main-text requirement.
review_limitations: The reviewed PDF SHA-256 matched the supplied PDF SHA-256.
